sanskrit: rudhirasyeva te gandhaḥ śavasyeva ca darśanam aśivaḥ śivasaṃkāśo mṛto jīvann ivāṭasi
english: Your odor is as of blood, and the sight of you is as of a corpse; though resembling one who is wholesome, you are inauspicious, and you wander about, dead, as though alive.

sanskrit: antarmṛtyur aśuddhātmā pāpam evānucintayan prabudhyase prasvapiṣi vartase carase sukhī
english: Inwardly dead, your soul unpurified, brooding upon evil alone, you wake, you sleep, you live, you move about at ease.

sanskrit: moghaṃ te jīvitaṃ rājan parikliṣṭaṃ ca jīvasi pāpāyeva ca sṛṣṭo 'si karmaṇe ha yavīyase
english: Vain is your life, O king, and in torment you live; it is for evil that you were created, for the basest of deeds.

sanskrit: bahu kalyāṇam icchanta īhante pitaraḥ sutān tapasā devatejyābhir vandanena titikṣayā
english: Desiring much good, fathers strive for sons through austerity, through sacrifices to the gods, through worship and through forbearance.

sanskrit: pitṛvaṃśam imaṃ paśya tvatkṛte narakaṃ gatam nirarthāḥ sarva evaiṣām āśābandhās tvadāśrayāḥ
english: Behold this line of your fathers, gone to hell on your account; fruitless are all the bonds of hope they had set upon you.

sanskrit: yān pūjayanto vindanti svargam āyur yaśaḥ sukham teṣu te satataṃ dveṣo brāhmaṇeṣu nirarthakaḥ
english: Toward those Brāhmaṇas, by honoring whom men obtain heaven, long life, fame, and happiness, your hatred is ceaseless and without purpose.

sanskrit: imaṃ lokaṃ vimucya tvam avāṅmūrdhā patiṣyasi aśāśvatīḥ śāśvatīś ca samāḥ pāpena karmaṇā
english: Quitting this world, you will fall headlong, through your sinful deeds, for years uncounted and years without end.

sanskrit: adyamāno jantugṛdhraiḥ śitikaṇṭhair ayomukhaiḥ tato 'pi punar āvṛttaḥ pāpayoniṃ gamiṣyasi
english: Devoured there by creatures and vultures, white-necked and iron-beaked; and even thence, returning once more, you will pass into a sinful womb.

sanskrit: yad idaṃ manyase rājan nāyam asti paraḥ kutaḥ pratismārayitāras tvāṃ yamadūtā yamakṣaye
english: As for your thought, O king, that there is no world beyond this—whence then?—the messengers of Yama, in Yama's abode, shall make you remember it well.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca evam uktaḥ pratyuvāca taṃ muniṃ janamejayaḥ garhyaṃ bhavān garhayati nindyaṃ nindati mā bhavān
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus addressed, Janamejaya answered that sage: 'What is blameworthy, you blame; what is censurable, you censure—do not so reproach me.'

sanskrit: dhikkāryaṃ mā dhikkurute tasmāt tvāhaṃ prasādaye sarvaṃ hīdaṃ svakṛtaṃ me jvalāmy agnāv ivāhitaḥ
english: You reproach me as one deserving reproach; therefore I seek your favor, for all this is my own doing, and I burn as though cast into the fire.

sanskrit: svakarmāṇy abhisaṃdhāya nābhinandati me manaḥ prāptaṃ nūnaṃ mayā ghoraṃ bhayaṃ vaivasvatād api
english: Looking back upon my own deeds, my mind takes no delight; surely a terror dreadful even beyond the son of Vivasvat has come upon me.

sanskrit: tat tu śalyam anirhṛtya kathaṃ śakṣyāmi jīvitum sarvamanyūn vinīya tvam abhi mā vada śaunaka
english: Without drawing out that barb, how shall I be able to live? Laying aside all your wrath, speak to me, O Śaunaka.

sanskrit: mahānasaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ bhaviṣyāmy arthavān punaḥ astu śeṣaṃ kulasyāsya mā parābhūd idaṃ kulam
english: I shall again become the cook-house of the Brāhmaṇas, rich in offerings; let there be a remnant of this house, let not this line be undone.

sanskrit: na hi no brahmaśaptānāṃ śeṣo bhavitum arhati śrutīr alabhamānānāṃ saṃvidaṃ vedaniścayāt
english: For of us, cursed by the Brāhmaṇas, no remnant ought to remain—of us who cannot grasp the sacred texts, nor the knowledge that comes from sure certainty of the Veda.

sanskrit: nirvidyamānaḥ subhṛśaṃ bhūyo vakṣyāmi sāṃpratam bhūyaś caivābhinaṅkṣanti nirdharmā nirjapā iva
english: Sorely afflicted, I shall speak yet again of what is fitting now; for again and again they perish, as men without dharma and without prayer.

sanskrit: arvāk ca pratitiṣṭhanti pulindaśabarā iva na hy ayajñā amuṃ lokaṃ prāpnuvanti kathaṃ cana
english: And they sink down low, like the Pulindas and Śabaras; for those who offer no sacrifice can in no way attain that world beyond.

sanskrit: avijñāyaiva me prajñāṃ bālasyeva supaṇḍitaḥ brahman piteva putrebhyaḥ prati māṃ vāñcha śaunaka
english: Without yet knowing my understanding, which is as a child's before the learned, O Brāhmaṇa, look kindly upon me, O Śaunaka, as a father upon his sons.

sanskrit: śaunaka uvāca kim āścaryaṃ yataḥ prājño bahu kuryād dhi sāṃpratam iti vai paṇḍito bhūtvā bhūtānāṃ nopatapyati
english: Śaunaka said: What wonder is it that a wise man should do much of what is fitting? Having become learned, he is not tormented on account of living beings.

sanskrit: prajñāprāsādam āruhya aśocyaḥ śocate janān jagatīsthān ivādristhaḥ prajñayā pratipaśyati
english: Mounting the palace of wisdom, himself beyond sorrow, he grieves for the multitude, and with his wisdom looks down upon them as one upon a mountain looks upon those who stand upon the earth.

sanskrit: na copalabhate tatra na ca kāryāṇi paśyati nirviṇṇātmā parokṣo vā dhikkṛtaḥ sarvasādhuṣu
english: Yet he does not grasp it there, nor does he see the things that ought to be done—being weary of soul, or remote, or held in reproach among all the good.

sanskrit: viditvobhayato vīryaṃ māhātmyaṃ veda āgame kuruṣveha mahāśāntiṃ brahmā śaraṇam astu te
english: Having known the power that lies on both sides, he knows the greatness that is in the scripture: attain here the great peace, and let Brahman be your refuge.

sanskrit: tad vai pāratrikaṃ cāru brāhmaṇānām akupyatām atha cet tapyase pāpair dharmaṃ ced anupaśyasi
english: Fair indeed is that other-worldly reward for those who do not anger the Brāhmaṇas—if you grieve for your sins, and if you look toward dharma.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca anutapye ca pāpena na cādharmaṃ carāmy aham bubhūṣuṃ bhajamānaṃ ca prativāñchāmi śaunaka
english: Janamejaya said: I grieve for my sin, and I practice no unrighteousness; and I in turn desire one who wishes me well and who serves me, O Śaunaka.

sanskrit: śaunaka uvāca chittvā stambhaṃ ca mānaṃ ca prītim icchāmi te nṛpa sarvabhūtahite tiṣṭha dharmaṃ caiva pratismara
english: Śaunaka said: Cutting away both stubbornness and pride, I desire your gladness, O king; abide in the welfare of all beings, and keep dharma in remembrance.

sanskrit: na bhayān na ca kārpaṇyān na lobhāt tvām upāhvaye tāṃ me devā giraṃ satyāṃ śṛṇvantu brāhmaṇaiḥ saha
english: Not from fear, nor from meanness, nor from greed do I call upon you; let the gods, together with the Brāhmaṇas, hear that my word is true.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ na kena cic cārthī tvāṃ ca dharmam upāhvaye krośatāṃ sarvabhūtānām aho dhig iti kurvatām
english: I, who seek nothing from anyone, call upon you and upon dharma, while all beings cry out, 'Alas! Shame!'

sanskrit: vakṣyanti mām adharmajñā vakṣyanty asuhṛdo janāḥ vācas tāḥ suhṛdaḥ śrutvā saṃjvariṣyanti me bhṛśam
english: Those who know not dharma will speak against me, and men who are no friends will speak against me; and my friends, hearing those words, will burn with great distress for me.

sanskrit: ke cid eva mahāprājñāḥ parijñāsyanti kāryatām jānīhi me kṛtaṃ tāta brāhmaṇān prati bhārata
english: Only some, of great wisdom, will understand what must be done; know what I have done, dear one, toward the Brāhmaṇas, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: yathā te matkṛte kṣemaṃ labheraṃs tat tathā kuru pratijānīhi cādrohaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ narādhipa
english: So act that on my account they may obtain security; and promise that you will do no harm to the Brāhmaṇas, O lord of men.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca naiva vācā na manasā na punar jātu karmaṇā drogdhāsmi brāhmaṇān vipra caraṇāv eva te spṛśe
english: Janamejaya said: Neither by word, nor by thought, nor ever again by deed shall I do harm to the Brāhmaṇas, O sage; I touch your very feet.

sanskrit: śaunaka uvāca tasmāt te 'haṃ pravakṣyāmi dharmam āvṛttacetase śrīmān mahābalas tuṣṭo yas tvaṃ dharmam avekṣase purastād dāruṇo bhūtvā sucitrataram eva tat
english: Śaunaka said: Therefore I shall declare to you, whose mind is turned back to it, the dharma—you who, prosperous, mighty, and content, now look toward dharma; and that, having first been harsh, is the more wondrous still.

sanskrit: anugṛhṇanti bhūtāni svena vṛttena pārthiva kṛtsne nūnaṃ sadasatī iti loko vyavasyati yatra tvaṃ tādṛśo bhūtvā dharmam adyānupaśyasi
english: Living beings show favor through their own conduct, O king; surely the whole world resolves what is good and what is bad accordingly—wherein you, having become such as you were, today look toward dharma.

sanskrit: hitvā suruciraṃ bhakṣyaṃ bhogāṃś ca tapa āsthitaḥ ity etad api bhūtānām adbhutaṃ janamejaya
english: That, forsaking most delicious food and enjoyments, one should take his stand in austerity—this too is a marvel among beings, O Janamejaya.

sanskrit: yo durbalo bhaved dātā kṛpaṇo vā tapodhanaḥ anāścaryaṃ tad ity āhur nātidūre hi vartate
english: That a weak man should be a giver, or a wretched one rich in austerity—this they call no wonder, for it stands not far off.

sanskrit: etad eva hi kārpaṇyaṃ samagram asamīkṣitam tasmāt samīkṣayaiva syād bhavet tasmiṃs tato guṇaḥ
english: For this very thing, when done wholly without reflection, is mere wretchedness; therefore let it be done with discernment, and thereby virtue will arise in it.

sanskrit: yajño dānaṃ dayā vedāḥ satyaṃ ca pṛthivīpate pañcaitāni pavitrāṇi ṣaṣṭhaṃ sucaritaṃ tapaḥ
english: Sacrifice, giving, compassion, the Vedas, and truth, O lord of the earth—these five are purifiers, and well-performed austerity is the sixth.

sanskrit: tad eva rājñāṃ paramaṃ pavitraṃ janamejaya tena samyag gṛhītena śreyāṃsaṃ dharmam āpsyasi
english: That very thing is the supreme purifier of kings, O Janamejaya; by rightly laying hold of it, you shall attain the more excellent dharma.

sanskrit: puṇyadeśābhigamanaṃ pavitraṃ paramaṃ smṛtam api hy udāharantīmā gāthā gītā yayātinā
english: Going to holy places is remembered as the supreme purifier; and indeed they recite these verses that were sung by Yayāti.

sanskrit: yo martyaḥ pratipadyeta āyur jīveta vā punaḥ yajñam ekāntataḥ kṛtvā tat saṃnyasya tapaś caret
english: The mortal who would set out, or would live out his span of life once more—let him, having performed sacrifice with single devotion, then renounce it and practice austerity.

sanskrit: puṇyam āhuḥ kurukṣetraṃ sarasvatyāṃ pṛthūdakam yatrāvagāhya pītvā vā naivaṃ śvomaraṇaṃ tapet
english: They call Kurukṣetra holy, and Pṛthūdaka upon the Sarasvatī, where, having bathed or drunk, one need not grieve over death on the morrow.

sanskrit: mahāsaraḥ puṣkarāṇi prabhāsottaramānase kālodaṃ tv eva gantāsi labdhāyur jīvite punaḥ
english: To Mahāsaras, to the Puṣkaras, to Prabhāsa and Uttaramānasa, and to Kālodaka indeed you shall go, having gained your span, to live again.

sanskrit: sarasvatīdṛṣadvatyau sevamāno 'nusaṃcareḥ svādhyāyaśīlaḥ sthāneṣu sarveṣu samupaspṛśeḥ
english: Resorting to the Sarasvatī and the Dṛṣadvatī, you should wander along them; devoted to the recitation of scripture, you should perform your ablutions at all the sacred sites.

sanskrit: tyāgadharmaṃ pavitrāṇāṃ saṃnyāsaṃ param abravīt atrāpy udāharantīmā gāthāḥ satyavatā kṛtāḥ
english: He declared renunciation, the dharma of giving up, to be the highest of purifiers; and here too they recite these verses made by Satyavat.

sanskrit: yathā kumāraḥ satyo vai na puṇyo na ca pāpakṛt na hy asti sarvabhūteṣu duḥkham asmin kutaḥ sukham
english: Even as a child, in truth, is neither doer of merit nor doer of sin—for in all beings there is no abiding sorrow, whence then could there be happiness?

sanskrit: evaṃ prakṛtibhūtānāṃ sarvasaṃsargayāyinām tyajatāṃ jīvitaṃ prāyo vivṛte puṇyapātake
english: So it is for those who are by nature thus, who go through every kind of contact, and who for the most part give up life, when merit and sin alike lie open before them.

sanskrit: yat tv eva rājño jyāyo vai kāryāṇāṃ tad vadāmi te balena saṃvibhāgaiś ca jaya svargaṃ punīṣva ca
english: But that which is the greater among the duties of a king, that I declare to you: by strength and by sharing out gifts, conquer heaven and purify yourself.

sanskrit: yasyaivaṃ balam ojaś ca sa dharmasya prabhur naraḥ brāhmaṇānāṃ sukhārthaṃ tvaṃ paryehi pṛthivīm imām
english: The man who has such strength and vigor is the lord of dharma; for the welfare of the Brāhmaṇas, do you traverse this earth.

sanskrit: yathaivainān purākṣaipsīs tathaivainān prasādaya api dhikkriyamāṇo 'pi tyajyamāno 'py anekadhā
english: Even as you once cast them down, so now win their favor, though you be reproached, though you be forsaken in many ways.

sanskrit: ātmano darśanaṃ vidvan nāhantāsmīti mā krudhaḥ ghaṭamānaḥ svakāryeṣu kuru naiḥśreyasaṃ param
english: Knowing the vision of the self, O learned one, be not angered with the thought 'I am not'; striving in your own duties, achieve the highest good.

sanskrit: himāgnighorasadṛśo rājā bhavati kaś cana lāṅgalāśanikalpo vā bhavaty anyaḥ paraṃtapa
english: One king there is who becomes dreadful as frost or fire; and another becomes like the plough or the thunderbolt, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: na niḥśeṣeṇa mantavyam acikitsyena vā punaḥ na jātu nāham asmīti prasaktavyam asādhuṣu
english: One must not think a man wholly lost, nor again as past all cure; nor should one ever cling, among the wicked, to the thought 'I am undone.'

sanskrit: vikarmaṇā tapyamānaḥ pādāt pāpasya mucyate naitat kāryaṃ punar iti dvitīyāt parimucyate cariṣye dharmam eveti tṛtīyāt parimucyate
english: Grieving over a wrong deed, one is freed from a quarter of the sin; resolving 'I shall not do this again,' he is freed from a second; resolving 'I shall practice dharma alone,' he is freed from a third.

sanskrit: kalyāṇam anumantavyaṃ puruṣeṇa bubhūṣatā ye sugandhīni sevante tathāgandhā bhavanti te ye durgandhīni sevante tathāgandhā bhavanti te
english: The good is to be approved by a man who wishes to prosper: those who frequent fragrant things become fragrant accordingly, and those who frequent foul-smelling things become foul accordingly.

sanskrit: tapaścaryāparaḥ sadyaḥ pāpād dhi parimucyate saṃvatsaram upāsyāgnim abhiśastaḥ pramucyate trīṇi varṣāṇy upāsyāgniṃ bhrūṇahā vipramucyate
english: One devoted to the practice of austerity is at once freed from sin; tending the fire for a year, the accused man is released; tending the fire for three years, even the slayer of an embryo is wholly freed.

sanskrit: yāvataḥ prāṇino hanyāt tajjātīyān svabhāvataḥ pramīyamāṇān unmocya bhrūṇahā vipramucyate
english: By delivering from death as many living beings of that same kind, by their own nature perishing, as he had slain, the slayer of an embryo is wholly freed.

sanskrit: api vāpsu nimajjeta trir japann aghamarṣaṇam yathāśvamedhāvabhṛthas tathā tan manur abravīt
english: Or he should plunge into the waters, reciting the Aghamarṣaṇa thrice; that is even as the final bath of the horse-sacrifice—so Manu declared.

sanskrit: kṣipraṃ praṇudate pāpaṃ satkāraṃ labhate tathā api cainaṃ prasīdanti bhūtāni jaḍamūkavat
english: Swiftly he drives away his sin, and likewise obtains honor; and toward him living beings grow gracious, even those dull and dumb.

sanskrit: bṛhaspatiṃ devaguruṃ surāsurāḥ; sametya sarve nṛpate 'nvayuñjan dharme phalaṃ vettha kṛte maharṣe; tathetarasmin narake pāpaloke
english: The gods and demons all together, O king, came to Bṛhaspati, the teacher of the gods, and questioned him: 'You know the fruit in dharma, when done, O great sage, and likewise in the other, in hell, the world of sin.'

sanskrit: ubhe tu yasya sukṛte bhavetāṃ; kiṃ svit tayos tatra jayottaraṃ syāt ācakṣva naḥ karmaphalaṃ maharṣe; kathaṃ pāpaṃ nudate puṇyaśīlaḥ
english: 'But for one in whom both good deeds should be present, which of the two would there prevail in victory? Tell us, O great sage, the fruit of works: how does one of virtuous conduct drive away sin?'

sanskrit: bṛhaspatir uvāca kṛtvā pāpaṃ pūrvam abuddhipūrvaṃ; puṇyāni yaḥ kurute buddhipūrvam sa tat pāpaṃ nudate puṇyaśīlo; vāso yathā malinaṃ kṣārayuktyā
english: Bṛhaspati said: Having first committed sin unwittingly, he who then performs meritorious deeds with deliberate purpose—such a one of virtuous conduct drives away that sin, as a soiled garment is cleansed by the use of lye.

sanskrit: pāpaṃ kṛtvā na manyeta nāham asmīti pūruṣaḥ cikīrṣed eva kalyāṇaṃ śraddadhāno 'nasūyakaḥ
english: Having done a sin, a man should not think 'I am undone'; rather, faithful and free of malice, he should ever wish to do good.

sanskrit: chidrāṇi vasanasyeva sādhunā vivṛṇoti yaḥ yaḥ pāpaṃ puruṣaḥ kṛtvā kalyāṇam abhipadyate
english: As one repairs the holes of a garment with good thread, so does the man who, having done a sin, takes up the doing of good.

sanskrit: yathādityaḥ punar udyaṃs tamaḥ sarvaṃ vyapohati kalyāṇam ācarann evaṃ sarvaṃ pāpaṃ vyapohati
english: As the sun, rising again, drives away all darkness, so one who practices good drives away all his sin.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca evam uktvā sa rājānam indroto janamejayam yājayām āsa vidhivad vājimedhena śaunakaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Having thus addressed king Janamejaya, Śaunaka of Indrota's line had him perform, according to rule, the horse-sacrifice.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rājā vyapanītakalmaṣaḥ; śriyā yutaḥ prajvalitāgnirūpayā viveśa rājyaṃ svam amitrakarśano; divaṃ yathā pūrṇavapur niśākaraḥ
english: Then that king, his stain removed, endowed with majesty in the likeness of blazing fire, entered his own kingdom, that wearer-down of foes, as the full-bodied moon enters the sky.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca śṛṇu pārtha yathāvṛttam itihāsaṃ purātanam gṛdhrajambukasaṃvādaṃ yo vṛtto vaidiśe purā
english: Bhīṣma said: Hear, O Pārtha, as it befell, an ancient tale—the dialogue of the vulture and the jackal that took place long ago at Vidiśā.

sanskrit: duḥkhitāḥ ke cid ādāya bālam aprāptayauvanam kulasarvasvabhūtaṃ vai rudantaḥ śokavihvalāḥ
english: Certain grief-stricken people, taking up a child who had not yet reached his youth—the very all-in-all of their family—wept, overwhelmed with sorrow.

sanskrit: bālaṃ mṛtaṃ gṛhītvātha śmaśānābhimukhāḥ sthitāḥ aṅkenāṅkaṃ ca saṃkramya rurudur bhūtale tadā
english: Having taken up the dead child, they stood facing the cremation-ground, and passing him from lap to lap, they wept then upon the ground.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ ruditaśabdena gṛdhro 'bhyetya vaco 'bravīt ekātmakam imaṃ loke tyaktvā gacchata māciram
english: At the sound of their weeping a vulture drew near and spoke these words: 'Leave this one whose single self has passed, and depart from the world of the living without delay.'

sanskrit: iha puṃsāṃ sahasrāṇi strīsahasrāṇi caiva hi samānītāni kālena kiṃ te vai jātv abāndhavāḥ
english: 'Here thousands of men, and thousands of women too, have been brought together by Time; how then could these ever be without kinsmen?'

sanskrit: saṃpaśyata jagat sarvaṃ sukhaduḥkhair adhiṣṭhitam saṃyogo viprayogaś ca paryāyeṇopalabhyate
english: 'Look upon the whole world, beset with pleasures and pains; union and separation are met with by turns.'

sanskrit: gṛhītvā ye ca gacchanti ye 'nuyānti ca tān mṛtān te 'py āyuṣaḥ pramāṇena svena gacchanti jantavaḥ
english: 'Those creatures who take up the dead and carry them, and those who follow after them, they too depart, each according to the measure of his own life-span.'

sanskrit: alaṃ sthitvā śmaśāne 'smin gṛdhragomāyusaṃkule kaṅkālabahule ghore sarvaprāṇibhayaṃkare
english: 'Enough of lingering in this cremation-ground, thronged with vultures and jackals, heaped with skeletons, dreadful, terrifying to all living beings.'

sanskrit: na punar jīvitaḥ kaś cit kāladharmam upāgataḥ priyo vā yadi vā dveṣyaḥ prāṇināṃ gatir īdṛśī
english: 'No one who has met the law of Time lives again, whether dear or hated; such is the course of living beings.'

sanskrit: sarveṇa khalu martavyaṃ martyaloke prasūyatā kṛtāntavihite mārge ko mṛtaṃ jīvayiṣyati
english: 'Everyone who is born into the world of mortals must surely die; upon the path ordained by the Ender, who shall bring the dead to life?'

sanskrit: karmāntavihite loke cāstaṃ gacchati bhāskare gamyatāṃ svam adhiṣṭhānaṃ sutasnehaṃ visṛjya vai
english: 'In a world where labor draws to its close, and as the sun is going down, let each go to his own abode, casting off his love for the son.'

sanskrit: tato gṛdhravacaḥ śrutvā vikrośantas tadā nṛpa bāndhavās te 'bhyagacchanta putram utsṛjya bhūtale
english: Then, having heard the vulture's words, those kinsmen, crying aloud, O king, set forth, abandoning the son upon the ground.

sanskrit: viniścityātha ca tataḥ saṃtyajantaḥ svam ātmajam nirāśā jīvite tasya mārgam āruhya dhiṣṭhitāḥ
english: And then, having made their resolve, forsaking their own offspring, despairing of his life, they set out upon the road and went their way.

sanskrit: dhvāṅkṣābhrasamavarṇas tu bilān niḥsṛtya jambukaḥ gacchamānān sma tān āha nirghṛṇāḥ khalu mānavāḥ
english: But a jackal, colored like a crow or a storm-cloud, coming forth from his hole, called out to them as they departed: 'Pitiless indeed are these mortals!'
